title: Time zone considerations when travelling
body:
I really want to love Apple Health, but the sleep tracking becomes frustratingly unreliable when traveling across time zones.

Right now, the app doesn’t properly adjust for time zone changes, which ends up distorting the data it stores. Sleep sessions get split, overlapped, or logged at incorrect times, making it look like I slept at odd hours or barely slept at all. This completely throws off trends, averages, and any long-term insights the app is supposed to provide.

For example, a full night’s sleep during a flight or after landing can appear as fragmented or misaligned data, simply because the app doesn’t reconcile the time difference properly. Over time, this creates inaccurate sleep history, making it hard to trust the metrics or use them for health decisions.

If Apple Health aims to be a reliable wellness tool, handling time zone transitions should be a basic feature. The app should automatically detect travel, normalize sleep data across time zones, and preserve the integrity of sleep duration and cycles regardless of location.

Until this is fixed, the sleep data feels inconsistent and unreliable—especially for frequent travelers.

title: Improve for women please
body:
The cycle tracking is not useful for perimenopause. There are no options to add HRT at all - it’s all focussed on one aspect of menstruation which is pregnancy. This feature in the app would appear to be a victim of a society where women have no other use than bearing children. It’s disappointing that cycle tracking is only useful for a small subset of women - once you hit peri don’t bother with this until it gets some major updates. Ideal would be to have ability to add symptoms to menstrual cycle tracking that aren’t in the standard list so users can track effect of hormone fluctuations on any health issue they have, and add HRT regimes (including testosterone) to track effect on symptoms. This could be a ground breaking addition to understanding many health conditions that are not well studied in women. 

Other aspects of the health app are quite good - having a link to various exercise equipment apps is good for tracking training. Step count goo& heart rate monitor etc.

title: So much room for improvement
body: For an innovative company, Apple are really missing the mark here. Creating an entry for any one of the features is not intuitive and there are so many limitations that the user is blocked by that it seems a total waste of time. For example, medications. You can’t edit the name once it’s been created. The mood tracking is too simplistic and doesn’t allow for nuances as mood is not always as simple as being a sliding scale from feeling ‘pleasant’ or ‘unpleasant’. And to make it more frustrating, when creating an entry the next day for the same thing, the app seems to have changed format and I can’t work out how to add an entry for today. There’s a bunch of links to read about mood etc that just take up space and fluff up what space could be used for what you actually expected to find. The data also is pretty much rendered useless because each chart has to be looked at independently. When really what you’re looking for is what all the data looks like across the time line in a simple graph. E.g Heart rate line on the Y axis, with another line above for mood, another line for medications etc. I’m really not sure what the app is trying to achieve other than farming data from what it can grab from linked devices for their own ‘research’. It’s confusing and not user friendly and I wonder each time I go back to try and use it why I bother 🤦‍♀️.

title: Generally very good
body:
Very good for a free app, in general it has helped me see data and try to better manage my health. 

One minor irritation is the medications part it gives you a list of options of tablet and spray and patch and gel etc but it doesn’t have an “other” option and does not include sublingual film medication. I don’t expect it to include something uncommon but an “other “ option would be ideal so you don’t have to use an inaccurate term. If you won’t have “other” then you need to include all the different forms of medication.  

Suppository is written as an option I presume PR (per rectal) but there is also not any option for PV (per vagina) meds which I would think quite common as are used in fertility treatments. Again it’s fine to not include every option. But why is there no “other “ option ? I’m sure that’s a fairly simple thing to do compared to the complex ways to measure heart rate etc. not that I expect anyone to read this, but that would be a very easy way to make an improvement

title: Sadly, does not work for complicated medication regimes
body:
I tried setting this up for my elderly mother who has many tablets to take each day. I was hoping it would reduce her mental burden, but all it has done is make my mum’s life way more complicated.
Firstly, it cannot accomodate half (broken) tablets. The shapes are also very limited (no oval!). There’s no differentiation between large and tiny pills. And it would be helpful to be able to add or show break lines down the centre. And the colour-coding… frustratingly, not one of the set colours provided even comes close to any of mum’s medications (There is no brown, pale blue, lime green, or speckled).
Being able to markup tablets with text would be helpful in differentiating different, but similar looking tablets that have writing on them.
After wasting a hour trying to set it all up, I am forced to abandon this app as it will surely cause my mother to accidentally overdose because of the poor UI. :(

title: Medical ID is great! More customisation would be good though.
body:
I love the idea of the medical ID and it being able to be accessed from the Lock Screen in emergencies. There’s some great info you can put in there, but there are a few things that would be helpful to add, especially given the way we use our phones for everything these days.

I’d love to see an addition to the medical ID for things like pets, to show if your pets may be left at home and need someone to check in on them, their preferred vets if they’re with you at the time of an accident etc. Could also apply to kids for any parents, especially single parents.

Having employer or school contact could also be helpful to ensure they’re notified if relevant.

Being able to flag sensory or communication issues and management tactics for people with neurodivergencies or other special needs could be helpful, and otherwise being able to make some basic notes or custom additions. If the key items like name, emergency contacts etc remain at the top, then this will always be the first and most prominent piece of information, so having other things underneath wouldn’t hurt.

title: Unnecessary Flaws and Omissions Limit Utility
body: This app has a lot of useful data that is compromised by three unnecessary flaws. 1) On the screen that shows HR range per day you can scroll back over previous days but the Y axis changes if the range is different on different days. This makes it impossible to get a visual senses of the trend of your hourly HR. The Y Axis should be controlled by a setting so that ppl can choose to have a fixed Y axis or a pointless and completely useless constantly changing one - you know, for ppl who don’t understand how graphs work and just want to look at a pretty picture.  2) The only solution to this constantly changing Y Axis is to painstakingly type the data into a spreadsheet and set up your own graph with a sensible not constantly changing Y Axis. There should be some way to dump the data from the app into a file format like CSV. 3) The app only shows min and max HR for each hour but the watch and app must have all the readings for each hour. The complete set of HR readings should be viewable in the app and shld be able to be dumped out to a file. When I first started using this app you could view all HR readings in a list view but then there was an upgrade and that view was removed. It should be put back. Apart from these annoying flaws it’s pretty OK.
